title: MlflowSpanHandler open_spans and _pending_spans are guarded by self.lock at every access
answers: race condition in LlamaIndex span handler pending spans
why is self.lock needed around pending spans in the llama_index tracer
concurrent LlamaIndex events lose or mis-parent spans
body:
Invariant: every read or write of MlflowSpanHandler._pending_spans and open_spans happens under `with self.lock`, including the event lookup in get_span_for_event, the parent lookup in new_span, insertion in prepare_to_exit_span, and removal in resolve_pending_stream_span.
What breaks if skipped: LlamaIndex can dispatch span events from several threads, so an unlocked insert or pop can race with a parent lookup and yield a missing or wrong parent span.
The lock is the same one used for the parent lookup, so new locking should reuse it rather than add another.
applies: Any new code in mlflow/llama_index/tracer.py that touches the open or pending span maps.
says: Concurrent requests cause trace steps to be missing or assigned to wrong parents.
Parallel execution creates scrambled trace trees where sub-tasks appear under unrelated calls.
Some operations randomly vanish from the trace viewer when multiple threads run simultaneously.
Fix race conditions that corrupt span relationships during simultaneous background tasks.
search: In mlflow/llama_index/tracer.py, every read and write of MlflowSpanHandler._pending_spans and open_spans must be synchronized under self.lock. This locking covers get_span_for_event, new_span, prepare_to_exit_span, and resolve_pending_stream_span to prevent multi-threaded event dispatch from racing and mis-parenting or dropping spans. New locking code must reuse self.lock rather than creating a separate lock.
